title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative: In 2022, with support from the ILO/EU Sustainable Supply Chains to Build Forward Better" project (SSCBFB) project, the Ministry of Labour, Industrial Relations, and Employment Creation (MLIREC) piloted a Strategic Compliance Plan (SCP) in the fishing sector to implement ILO Work in Fishing Convention, 2007 (No.188). a. The issues covered in the SCP include overtime, meal intervals and rest periods and were selected by tripartite partners in the fishing sector through the National Technical Advisory Council (NTAC) of the project. The issues respond to the Covid-19 pandemic in terms of the safety and well-being of fishers, including their ability to leave ships to rest and or work overtime. b. In November 2022, the first ever joint labour inspection was successfully conducted in by the MLIREC, the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources (MFMR) and the Ministry of Works and Transport (MWT), directly benefiting 306 fishermen on board fishing vessels, 294 workers employed by fishing companies and 12 vessel managers. c. The SCP assisted the Labour inspectorate under the Directorate of Labour Services (DLS) to ensure the enforcement of general working conditions (working time, wages, unfair dismissal, employment of children and young persons) in the sector and to promote compliance and enforcement. d. The SCP resulted in the drafting of model contracts for fixed term and indefinite term contracts for fishermen in line with provisions from national legislation and C188.In March 2023, MLIREC gazetted a variation of chapter 3 of the Labour Act, with provisions to enhance decent working conditions for fishers-including total ordinary working hours, overtime, meal intervals, daily spread-over, and weekly rest period in line with the ILO Work in Fishing Convention, 2007 (No.188). In July 2023, MLIREC launched a social media campaign encompassing information dissemination and dialogue with social partners on the practical application of these new provisions. 1.In 2022, the ILO/EU Sustainable Supply Chains to Build Forward Better" project (SSCBFB) project organized a workshop to improve coordination among the relevant authorities and to strengthen their ability to apply a SCP approach to inspection in the fishing sector. As a result of the workshop, a Strategic Compliance Taskforce was created with 12 members from the tripartite partners. 2. In 2022, a toolkit on the fisheries supply chain was developed. It contains tools, instruments and guidelines on the fundamental principles and rights at work, the relevant international labour standards, the inspection of labour conditions on board fishing vessels and responsible business conduct: Namibia Field Guide on Labour Inspection On Board Fishing Vessels; two leaflets, on “Basic Employment Conditions for Decent Work” and “How to Stay Safe While Working On a Fishing Vessel At Sea”. The materials were handed over to the MLIREC and inspectors were trained on the use of this material in their work to improve conditions in the industry. 3. IN 2022, a training programme on OSH provisions on fishing vessels concluded with certification of 42 labour inspectors, shop stewards, fisheries inspectors, and fisheries observers from the harbour of Walvis Bay and Lüderitz. 4. In 2023, a Sensitization and Training Workshops on ILO Conventions No. 188 and 190 for fisheries stakeholders in Namibia were organized. 5. A Basic Safety and Familiarization training was organized for 15 labour and industry inspectors from the MLIREC to equip them with the necessary skills and certification to conduct inspections on board vessels. The training lasted one month and was conducted by the Namibian Maritime and Fisheries Institute. 6.Tailored content on key provisions of the variation was developed and formulated into a three-month campaign new using the ILO’s Social Media for Labour Law Compliance Toolkit, and lessons learnt from a training on social media in December 2022.

description.narrative: The ILO’s Decent Work Results Dashboard –complementing the ILO’s Programme Implementation Report – presents information on the results achieved and on the most significant outputs delivered by the ILO during the relevant biennium.

description.narrative: The ILO’s Results Framework is always part of the Programme and Budget (P&B) document for the relevant biennium. Please refer to the Annex “Results Framework” of the relevant P&B Document

The ILO’s biennial Programme Implementation Report is an instrument of accountability. It describes the performance of the Organization against the commitments made in the Programme and Budget documents for the corresponding biennial period.
